A01: Ambiguous or executable YAML lets a node mean different things to different loaders, so the next session cannot trust the graph.
A02: A contract stored off the canonical path is invisible to routing; the next session rediscovers the boundary by searching source.
A03: One explicit owner lets this repository route each responsibility consistently.
A04: A forbidden parent-child kind pair is a graph the walk cannot write and later sessions cannot navigate.
A05: Composition state is how an agent knows whether to look for children or stop.
A06: An unreachable or cyclic composition graph has no top-down route from the repository.
A07: Keeping declared child units under their parent makes composition agree with filesystem ownership; this does not prove worker write confinement.
A08: A dangling dependency is a promised edge that leads nowhere.
A09: A dependency cycle makes change order undefined.
A10: A boundary without a declared surface has no legal entry, so callers invent one.
A11: A declared path that does not exist is a lie the next session will follow.
A12: One-sided invariant/verification links leave truth unproven or checks that prove nothing named.
A13: A binding without a registered detector is a rule nobody can fail.
A14: Two nodes claiming the same owns hide which contract to route to.
A15: A technical-layer module name is a horizontal slice, not a capability an agent can own.
A16: A utils or helpers name is a bag, not a responsibility, so routing cannot terminate.
P01-01: This product's provider receives integer minor units.
